title: Gauss-norm completeness and variable regrouping of restricted series
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, complete for $d(x,y)=|x-y|$. For $n\ge0$, let $D_n=F\langle T_1,\ldots,T_nangle$ be the restricted-series subring of [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]: its elements are coefficient families $f=\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^n}c_
u T^
u$ for which, for each $\epsilon>0$, only finitely many $
u$ have $|c_
u|\ge\epsilon$; addition is coefficientwise and multiplication is the finite Cauchy product in each coefficient. Put $\|f\|=\sup_
u|c_
u|$. This is a finite-valued norm, $\|f\|=0$ exactly when $f=0$, $\|1\|=1$, $\|-f\|=\|f\|$, $\|f+g\|\le\max(\|f\|,\|g\|)$ and $\|fg\|\le\|f\|\|g\|$. The metric $\|f-g\|$ on $D_n$ is complete, and the finite truncations $\sum_{
u_1+\cdots+
u_n\le N}c_
u T^
u$ converge to $f$ in this metric. For $s\ge0$, grouping coefficients by the last variable $X$ identifies $D_{s+1}$, as a ring and isometrically, with the series $\sum_{i\ge0}a_iX^i$ with $a_i\in D_s$ and $\|a_i\|	o0$, equipped with coefficientwise addition, Cauchy product and norm $\sup_i\|a_i\|$. Here $D_0=F$, and the identification preserves constants and multiplication by $X$.

proof.text: For multiplication in [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation], the coefficient at $\gamma$ is $\sum_{\alpha+\beta=\gamma}c_\alpha d_\beta$, a finite sum since each coordinate of $\alpha$ is bounded by that of $\gamma$. Induction on the number of summands gives $|\sum b_j|\le\max_j|b_j|$ from the assumed ultrametric inequality; hence each product coefficient is at most $\|f\|\|g\|$ and taking the supremum proves the product bound. To check restrictedness directly, put $M=\max(1,\|f\|,\|g\|)$. The sets $S=\{\alpha:|c_\alpha|\ge\epsilon/M\}$ and $T=\{\beta:|d_\beta|\ge\epsilon/M\}$ are finite. Outside the finite set $S+T=\{\alpha+\beta:\alpha\in S,\beta\in T\}$, every summand has one factor smaller than $\epsilon/M$ and the other at most $M$, so the finite sum has absolute value smaller than $\epsilon$. This verifies closure without using a completeness theorem. The inherited formal-series ring operations therefore have all the asserted norm bounds.

proof.text:
For finite truncations, given $\epsilon>0$ take the finite set $S=\{
u:|c_
u|\ge\epsilon/2\}$. Choose $N_0$ at least the total degree $
u_1+\cdots+
u_n$ of every element of $S$ (zero if $S$ is empty). For $N\ge N_0$ every omitted coefficient has absolute value smaller than $\epsilon/2$, so the supremum of the omitted coefficients is at most $\epsilon/2<\epsilon$. There are only finitely many multi-indices of total degree at most $N$, since each coordinate lies in $\{0,\ldots,N\}$. These are exactly the specified finite truncations and they converge to $f$.

proof.text: Use the coordinate bijection $\mathbf N^{s+1}=\mathbf N^s\times\mathbf N$, and set $a_i=\sum_\mu c_{\mu,i}T^\mu$. Each row is restricted because its $\epsilon$-exceptional set is a slice of the finite exceptional set of $c$. For $\epsilon>0$ project the finite set $\{(\mu,i):|c_{\mu,i}|\ge\epsilon/2\}$ onto the last coordinate. Outside this finite projection every row norm is at most $\epsilon/2$, proving $\|a_i\|\to0$. Conversely, if each row is restricted and $\|a_i\|\to0$, then only finitely many rows have norm at least $\epsilon$; only these rows can contain a coefficient of absolute value at least $\epsilon$, and in each such row there are only finitely many of them. Their finite union proves global restrictedness. The inverse is therefore the coefficient assignment $c_{\mu,i}=(a_i)_\mu$. Moreover $\sup_{\mu,i}|c_{\mu,i}|=\sup_i\sup_\mu|c_{\mu,i}|$: both sides are the least common upper bound of precisely the same coefficient values. Applied to differences this gives the claimed isometry.

source.place: Agent coefficient proof below; BGR not locally available, as recorded in the statement source and report. No unverified BGR theorem number is asserted.

proof.text: The coefficient bijection of step 6 preserves addition. For products, its coefficient at $(\mu,k)$ is $\sum_{i+j=k}\sum_{\alpha+\beta=\mu}c_{\alpha,i}d_{\beta,j}$ on either side, by the finite Cauchy-product formula of [def-trf-restricted-series-presentation]. Both sums are finite, so regrouping them is a finite distributive-law calculation. In particular the iterated Cauchy product is restricted by step 2 after the inverse assignment; no infinite rearrangement is involved. A constant has only coefficient $(0,0)$, and multiplication by $X$ changes $c_{\mu,0}$ to zero and $c_{\mu,i+1}$ to the old $c_{\mu,i}$. These formulas prove both final compatibilities. For $n=0$ the index set $\mathbf N^0$ is a singleton, so $D_0=F$ with its original absolute value; all arguments, including $s=0$, apply.
